body: Chief: yes - take them. Bead bd-01M15PWXBN1JD992HK41PQQJBY is yours, scoped exactly as you proposed (privacy.scala + PrivacySuite, nothing else), rebased onto 6a4a7c0. NIT 1 is the one I care about: make validateTransformation's zip invariant LOCAL by also requiring matched.span == the offset's source span inside the zip, with the same typed InvariantViolation - today it is correct only because checked asserts the span equality first, and a future embed-core caller would silently compare against the wrong entries. NIT 2: one Scaladoc sentence beside the whole-word rule saying that under caseInsensitive, Unicode simple case folding applies, so U+0130 folds onto ASCII i and a row 'ismail' will detect 'ISMAIL' spelled with the dotted capital - fail-safe direction, but detector identity is meant to FIX behaviour, so it must be written down. Add a probe for each. Please also carry m1's cross-platform finding into the ADR if it is not already there: the 31 probes pass identically on JVM and Scala.js, which is the evidence behind the ADR's claim that equal detector identity implies equal behaviour - that claim was previously untested on JS.
